pm_exper_user_4672_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Because you often manage spring allergies, you might want to schedule outdoor activities when pollen levels are lowest and wear a breathable face covering to reduce exposure. Carrying your usual antihistamine and taking breaks in shaded or less windy spots can also help you stay comfortable all day.
(b) Since spring tends to trigger your seasonal allergic rhinitis, it can help to check pollen counts before heading out and plan your time outdoors for lower-pollen hours, like after rainfall. Wearing a light mask and keeping your antihistamines on hand can make long stretches outside much more comfortable.
(c) It’s a good idea to check the weather forecast before spending long periods outdoors and dress in layers so you can adjust to changing temperatures. Taking occasional breaks in shaded areas and staying hydrated will help you feel comfortable throughout the day.
(d) Since you sometimes deal with spring pollen flare-ups from your seasonal allergic rhinitis, plan your time outdoors during calmer, post-rain periods and keep antihistamines handy. You could also bring along a thermos of freshly brewed oolong tea to sip while enjoying the scenery for an extra touch of comfort.
